title: Why a heavy suitcase is hardest to push at the start
examples: Why is it harder to start pushing something than to keep it moving?
Is sliding friction smaller than static friction?

forces.label: Your push
forces.ask: Why is it hardest to get it moving?

explain.say: Have you ever pushed a heavy suitcase across an airport floor in Tokyo? The first shove is the hardest, then it suddenly slides more easily. Why? Friction, which means a force that tries to stop surfaces sliding past each other.

draw.text: Why a heavy suitcase is hardest to push at the start

forces.label: Your push
forces.ask: Why is it hardest to get it moving?

explain.say: See your push arrow, pointing right? The arrow pointing left is static friction, the friction when nothing is sliding yet. Right now the two are exactly equal, so the case stays still. Are the arrows the same size?

forces.label: Your push
forces.ask: Why is it hardest to get it moving?

explain.say: Yes, they are! Static friction is clever: it grows to match your push, up to a limit. Tiny bumps on the case and the floor lock together like teeth. Push harder than that limit, and the bumps break free. What happens then?

forces.label: Your push
forces.ask: Why is it hardest to get it moving?

explain.say: It slides! Now look at the left arrow: sliding friction, and it is smaller. Moving bumps do not lock together so well. So your same push is now bigger than friction, and the case speeds up. Which arrow is bigger now?

forces.label: Your push
forces.ask: Why is it hardest to get it moving?

explain.say: Your push, great spotting! That is why it suddenly feels easier. Wow fact: anti-lock car brakes pulse on and off so the tyres keep gripping instead of skidding, because gripping friction is stronger than sliding friction. Try pushing a heavy book and feel the moment it lets go.

faq.q: Why is it hardest to get it moving?
faq.a: Before it moves, static friction can grow quite large. Once it slides, friction drops to a smaller sliding value, so less push is needed.
asks: Why is starting to push harder than keeping it moving?

faq.a: Static friction holds two surfaces still against each other. It matches your push up to a maximum, called limiting friction.
Sliding friction, also called kinetic friction, acts while surfaces slide past each other. It is usually a bit smaller than the maximum static friction.
Rougher surfaces and pressing the surfaces together harder, for example a heavier case, both increase friction.

faq.q: Why do cars have anti-lock brakes?
faq.a: If wheels lock and skid, only sliding friction acts and steering is lost. Anti-lock brakes keep the tyres gripping, which stops the car better.

facts: Maximum static friction is usually larger than sliding (kinetic) friction for the same surfaces.
Anti-lock braking systems stop wheels locking so tyres keep their grip.

quiz.say: A box stays still while you push it with 30 N. How big is the friction?
quiz.show: A box stays still while you push it with 30 N. How big is the friction?
quiz.why: The box is still, so the forces are balanced: friction equals your 30 newton push.

wrong.0: With no friction, your push would make it move.
wrong.1: Friction only matches your push; it never pushes the box backwards.

quiz.say: Once a box starts sliding, friction usually…
quiz.show: Once a box starts sliding, friction usually…
quiz.why: Sliding friction is normally less than the maximum static friction.

wrong.1: Sliding friction is usually smaller than the starting limit.
wrong.2: Sliding friction still acts; it is just a bit weaker.
